title: Soft Lithographic Procedure for Producing Plastic Microfluidic Devices with View-ports Transparent to Visible and Infrared Light
protocol: Prepare a photomask for the primary mold using standard optical mask fabrication procedures if not available from independent providers.
Spin coat a 4 inch silicon wafer with SU-8 3010 negative photoresist at 2,300 rpm for 30 seconds.
Soft-bake the photoresist on a hot plate first at 65 °C for 2 minutes and then at 95 °C for 8 minutes.
Expose the photoresist to UV light (i-line, 365 nm) through the photomask under the mask aligner with a total energy dose of 100-120 mJ/cm² using hard contact mode.
Post exposure bake the wafer at 65 °C for 1 minute and then at 95 °C for 2 minutes.
Develop the photoresist using SU-8 developer at room temperature, rinse with isopropyl alcohol, and gently blow dry with nitrogen.
Treat the silicon mold with oxygen plasma at 60 W for 30 seconds with a flow rate of 20 sccm of oxygen.
Set the chamber pressure to 1-10 mbar during the silanization process.
Place the mold in a vacuum jar with 50 μL of silane.
Maintain the jar under vacuum (1-10 mbar) for at least 2 hours.
Mix PDMS elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 10:1.
Degas the mixture by leaving it in a vacuum jar under vacuum (1-10 mbar) for approximately 15 minutes or until no visible bubbles remain.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture onto the silicon mold.
Heat at 70 °C for 2 hours on a hot plate to cure the PDMS.
Remove the cured PDMS from the hot plate and let it cool down to room temperature.
Cut the cooled PDMS along the edges of the silicon mold with a razor blade.
Pinch one corner of the cut PDMS with tweezers.
Carefully peel the PDMS replica off the silicon mold.
Treat the PDMS mold with oxygen plasma at 60 W for 30 s with 20 sccm of oxygen flow.
Set the chamber pressure to 1-10 mbar during silanization.
Place the mold in a vacuum jar with 50 µL of silane.
Leave the jar in the vacuum state (1-10 mbar) for at least 2 h.
Mix the PDMS elastomer and curing agent in a ratio of 10:1.
Degas the mixture by leaving it in a vacuum jar at 1-10 mbar for approximately 15 minutes or until no visible bubbles remain.
Pour the degassed PDMS mixture on acrylic templates, ensuring their top-most surface is submerged about 1 mm below the liquid surface.
Degas the PDMS again to remove any trapped air with the same settings as previously used.
Heat the PDMS at 60 °C for 2 hours on a leveled hot plate to cure the mixture.
Remove the cured PDMS from the hot plate and let it cool down to room temperature.
Cut the PDMS along the edges of the acrylic templates using a razor blade.
Pinch one corner of the cut PDMS with a pair of tweezers and carefully peel the PDMS off the acrylic templates.
Treat the CaF2 window with oxygen plasma at 60 W for 30 seconds with a flow of 20 sccm of oxygen.
Place the first PDMS template on a flat surface, such as a soda lime plate.
Position a CaF2 window centered on top of the PDMS plug and gently press to ensure good contact.
Place a thin UV-transparent plate on the backside of the PDMS mold, aligned with the central chamber location.
Ensure that the quartz plate is in good contact with the PDMS mold.
Align all elements (template, mold, and window) such that they are in good contact and properly aligned.
Gradually dispense drops of NOA at the inlet of the PDMS template.
Allow the resin to slowly fill the cavity until it comes into contact with the edge of the CaF2 window.
Capillary flow will then fill the thin gap (~10 µm) between the PDMS mold and CaF2 window.
Cure the NOA by exposure to UV light using a UV-LED exposure system for around 90 seconds at 100% power and continuous exposure mode.
Remove the thin quartz plate from the back of the PDMS mold carefully after curing.
Gently peel the PDMS mold from the top of the NOA layer.
Carefully remove the NOA layer from the PDMS template.
Treat the CaF2 window with oxygen plasma at 60 W for 30 seconds with a flow rate of 20 sccm of oxygen.
Place the second PDMS template on a flat surface such as a soda lime plate.
Center a CaF2 window on top of the PDMS plug and gently press it into good contact with the plug.
Place a 1 mm thick PDMS sheet aligned with the center of the PDMS template on top of the CaF2 window, ensuring good contact between the sheet and the window.
Gradually dispense drops of NOA at the inlet of the PDMS template to let it slowly fill the cavity.
Expose NOA to UV light for curing.
Peel off the PDMS sheet from the top of the NOA layer.
Carefully remove the cured NOA layer from the PDMS template.
Align both halves of the device such that CaF2 windows are aligned.
Gently finger-press both halves at the corner of the NOA layers to fix their position.
Cut two circular discs out of a 1 mm thick PDMS sheet using an 8 mm diameter puncher.
Cut two rectangles with the same size as the device (4 cm x 2.5 cm) from a 1 mm thick PDMS sheet.
On both PDMS rectangles, cut openings corresponding to the channels and in-let/out-let of the device.

Stack in the following order: one PDMS rectangle with pre-cut openings, one PDMS disc contacting the bottom window, the two finger-pressed halves of the device, the second PDMS disc sitting on the top window, and lastly the second PDMS rectangle with pre-cut openings.
Place the assembly in the vacuum press setup between two plates.
Seal the plastic bag containing the assembly.
Turn on the vacuum pump and evacuate the assembly.
Maintain evacuation for at least 10 minutes or until the base pressure is reached.
Expose the evacuated assembly to UV light from a broad-band Hg gas lamp at 270 W for 15 min.
Turn off the vacuum pump once exposure is complete.
Allow the assembly to slowly vent back to atmospheric pressure before removal.
